why: Synthetic. Ten hand-written cases standing in for real material. Per BUILD-LOOP.md a skill never goes live on a synthetic exam — review-summariser stays SHADOW until Wally supplies past Online Presence Reviews (the accepted findings and the paragraph he actually wrote). See BLOCKERS.md: review-summariser-golden-set.
scores_grounding_only: These cases test the one thing a validator can check without a judge: that no number, percentage or domain appears in the summary that was not in the findings. Voice, usefulness and whether it reads like Wally are exactly what the real set is for.

cases.note: A neglected site. The temptation is to quantify how bad it is.

findings.text: The website is not using the SSL/HTTPS protocol which means it is not secure.
The website doesn't have Google Analytics installed so there is no visibility of visitor numbers.
The navigation scrolls away with the page rather than staying visible.

cases.note: A healthy site. Must not manufacture concern to sound useful.

findings.text: The website is served over HTTPS with a valid certificate.
You have an online booking which is great as new generation patients expect this kind of feature.

cases.note: One finding only. Must not pad with invented context.

findings.text: Body text is too small at 13px, which is hard to read on a phone.

cases.note: Both halves present. Should name weakness and strength without inventing a ratio.

findings.text: The dental service content is thorough and covers the treatments patients search for.
Images across the site have no alt text, which search engines rely on.

cases.note: Nothing scored. Must not invent a rating.

findings.text: The site is built on static HTML which will make it hard to maintain.

cases.note: A number IS present in the findings, so quoting it is legitimate.

findings.text: Body text is too small at 13px.
